signature_moves: Cursor-as-mascot: the classic 1930s white four-fingered cartoon glove (Mickey/Cuphead lineage) literally IS the macOS pointer the app enhances — product function and brand mark are the same object
Comic 'impact' speed-lines radiating from the fingertip encode the product's attention-capture promise pictorially
Heavy black keyline + rubber-hose curves commit hard to a retro-cartoon playful register
Icon reads legacy-glossy (beveled specular sheen, dark keyline, full-bleed motif) — pre-Big-Sur skeuomorphic, NOT Liquid Glass / Icon Composer layered grammar
defects: No UI-surface defects loggable — no interface supplied; absence of defects is a coverage gap, not a clean bill of health
Icon (provisional, pending Workflow B) — full-bleed glossy off-centre motif likely misses current macOS icon conventions (centred glyph, layered material, no baked gloss)

aesthetic.direction: Playful / toy family crossed with 1930s rubber-hose cartoon; drenched single-hue color strategy (design-craft: 'Committed'/'Drenched', heavy keyline, sticker rendering)
peers: cursor/presentation utilities: Presentify, Mousepose, Cursor Pro
aesthetic.cluster_hint: retro-cartoon consumer brand (brand/icon-level only; NOT a macOS-native UI cluster — no native surface observed)

psychology: Von Restorff / isolation effect — the product's entire premise ('the most memorable thing on the call') IS the isolation effect; the brand mark (impact rays around one raised finger) visualizes making the cursor the single different, attention-grabbing element

Peripheral-vision attention capture (Weinschenk) — motion/pop in the periphery hijacks where eyes go next; the cursor-highlight product weaponizes exactly this, and the cover's speed-lines advertise it
First-impression 50ms appeal (Lindgaard) — saturated single-hue orange + one bold motif reads instantly as a poster/thesis statement
notes: CRITICAL for synthesis: neither supplied image is a macOS UI screenshot. cover.jpg is a pure brand illustration (orange gradient + white-gloved comic pointing hand + impact rays; no window/chrome/controls/text); icon.png is the app icon. Therefore NO framework lineage, era, or UI rubric could be assessed, and rubric_score/native_audit_score of 0 mean 'not applicable / not gradable', NOT 'scored and failed' — do not average these zeros into any UI quality statistic. All tokens are brand tokens, not design-system tokens, and must never feed macOS canon or a native style cluster. Pokey is a Communication-category app whose function (per tagline) is cursor highlighting for calls/screen-share — most likely a menu-bar-utility with an overlay-based UI — but that app class is INFERENCE, not evidence. The icon warrants a separate Workflow B (12-point icon) digest. To make this a real UI digest, a future pass needs at least one screenshot of an actual Pokey surface (menu-bar popover, settings, or the cursor overlay).
